actions.action: Prune the oldest, lowest brown/dry/yellow leaves at the base of the petiole with clean pruners
Move the plant gradually to the brightest spot over 1–2 weeks
Check the soil and water thoroughly when the top 2–3 inches are dry
Empty standing water from the outer pot or saucer and make sure the inner pot drains
Feed with balanced liquid fertilizer every 4–6 weeks in spring and summer
Bring the plant indoors before temperatures drop below 50°F
Repot one size up when roots fill the pot

reason: The answer correctly sees normal aging of the outer leaves and recommends pruning the lowest old leaves, but it limits cutting to mostly brown leaves and says to keep the tattered green ones, while the poster removed seven ragged lower leaves; nothing it suggests is likely to harm the plant.
